with-catspeak-amulet-prior-to-a-tail-of-.player: Well, my name is [player name] and I'm pleased to meet you. So, now that I'm not a stranger anymore, what's your name?

with-catspeak-amulet-prior-to-a-tail-of-.npc: Hmm... Nice to meet you, [player name]. I'm Neite.

options.text: How come you're the only cat around here?

steps.player: How come you're the only cat around here?

steps.npc: Oh there's far more than just me. The others are just shy. We do also get visitors from outside the city sometimes, like that Bob. He's quite a handsome beast...

steps.player: Oh, I see. Romance is in the air, is it?

steps.npc: Well, life here in the desert can be a lonely existence, even with all my busy work... Still, to be honest, he worries me.

steps.player: In what way?

steps.npc: Well, I pride myself on my knowledge of the family lines of cats. Obviously, Bob features quite heavily in most family trees, but he himself has none!

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.npc: Nobody is sure where he came from. Not even the Sphinx knows. It's just one of those mysteries.

steps.player: Interesting...
What are you doing?

steps.npc: I'm hunting frogs and locusts.

steps.player: Why? Do they taste good?

steps.npc: Yuck! No, I would never debase myself to eat such filth.

steps.player: I see you're a cat of taste then.

steps.npc: I am a cat of high breeding! My family tree dates back before those of any ruler on Gielinor.

steps.player: What do you do with the frogs and locusts?

steps.npc: What do you mean by 'do'?

steps.player: Well, seeing as you're hunting them, I thought you'd eat them too.

steps.npc: No, no, I just hunt them, play with them for a bit and then kill them.

steps.player: Isn't that a little evil?

steps.npc: What's evil about a little destruction?

steps.player: What isn't? You destroy and take away life. What good is there in that?

steps.npc: Life can come from destruction too. Take a volcano. It will destroy all life that surrounds it, but it will also fertilise and enrich the surrounding earth.
From that earth, more life will spring forth than there was in the first place.

steps.player: How do you compare killing frogs to a volcano? A volcano has no choice about whether it explodes or not, but you do have a choice.

steps.npc: I disagree. It's in my nature to prey on smaller life forms in the same way as it is in the volcanoes nature to explode.

steps.player: Don't they sometimes call the Devourer the goddess of destruction? You seem to have a lot in common with a goddess that your kind oppose.

steps.npc: That is not too surprising. A long time ago, I served her. Her form has changed a lot since then, just as mine has.

steps.player: You mean you weren't always a cat?

steps.npc: No, I used to be human. At the time when Amascut became the Devourer, I was one of her chief priestesses.

steps.player: So you stopped serving her because of that change?

steps.npc: Not initially. Many of us tolerated her new habits for some time. She went too far though, so we took action.

steps.player: What did you do?

steps.npc: The last of her priestesses gathered and cursed her. Unfortunately, she also cast a spell of her own, condemning us to an eternity of walking Gielinor in her form.

steps.player: So she's a cat then?

steps.npc: She's as much of a cat as Icthlarin is a dog.

steps.player: What curse did you cast upon her?

steps.npc: We trapped her in a human form, limiting her power. We also cursed her to never be willing worshipped again, though I fear that curse has started to wane.

steps.player: So that's why she's scared of cats?

steps.npc: Indeed. There are fewer of us priestesses left now, but we still hold enough power to be quite the problem for her.

options.text: Do you talk to the Sphinx much?

steps.player: Do you talk to the Sphinx much?

steps.npc: Not really. She is normally too wrapped up in preserving her immortality to be making conversation.

steps.player: So you don't like her then?

steps.npc: Nothing of the sorts. I have nothing but respect for her.

steps.player: Why is that?

steps.npc: Well, because her immortality is based on the fact that she keeps us cats safe. Her whole existence is dedicated to protecting us.

steps.player: That doesn't seem like much of a life.

steps.npc: True. Life shouldn't be hoarded, but lived. Of course, don't tell her I said that, otherwise I'd have to be on the lookout for a new guardian.

options.text: Tell me about you and the Devourer.

steps.player: Tell me about you and the Devourer.

steps.npc: Before she was the goddess of destruction, she was Amascut, the goddess of rebirth. Back then, I was human, and I served as one of her chief priestesses.
When she became the Devourer, many of us tolerated her new habits for some time. After all, destruction was key to being the goddess of rebirth, so it was something we were comfortable with.

steps.player: But she went too far?

steps.npc: Yes, so we took action. The last of her priestesses gathered and cursed her. Unfortunately, she also cast a spell of her own, condemning us to an eternity of walking Gielinor in her form.
Our curse trapped her in a human form, limiting her power. We also cursed her to never be willing worshipped again, though I fear that curse has started to wane.

steps.player: So that's why she's scared of cats?

steps.npc: Indeed. There are fewer of us priestesses left now, but we still hold enough power to be quite the problem for her.

steps.player: I'll leave you to it.
Where's Bob?

steps.text: Before Bob's trip to Sophanem in Dragon Slayer II:

steps.npc: Out gallivanting. I think he's hunting noobs in the Wilderness this time. You know what he's like.

steps.player: So, why aren't you out there with him?

steps.npc: I like to roam as much as the next cat, but, every so often, I do like to come home.

steps.player: So, you and Bob haven't had an argument?

steps.npc: Who told you that?

steps.player: Er... nobody.

steps.text: During Bob's trip to Sophanem in Dragon Slayer II:

steps.npc: He's meant to be with you. You haven't lost him have you?

steps.player: I don't think so.

steps.npc: Well keep an eye on him for me.
